summary: This rewrite stage combines pieces that were each measured separately (s2 Q/O, the warp top-k R and the NF=1 unpool) on top of the not-yet-run sk two-level parent. The design can reach its targets, but the full decode_1 estimate counts the o_norm_gate removal twice, and the sliding decode_1 kill line sits inside run-to-run drift. Proceed with no companion runs, and attribute through the per-piece prepare-time selector lines.
justification: The mechanism is plausible. At T=1 the replaced work is bound by weight reads and launch count. s2's dl_qkv_kernel streamed the 2304x8192 qkv_gate at 4.5 TB/s (8.3 us), and nvjet qkv + qk_norm + FP8 casts + store_cache are separate launches on master (kernel_fn lines ~2475-2495). The s2 run c6cb53d8 moved full decode_1 142.93 -> 137.98 (+4.65%, gained), and stack-route-topk-pdl-unpool-nf1 (87211e13) moved sliding decode_1 127.48 -> 122.44 and full decode_1 142.93 -> 136.93. Current master is 123.9 / 139.2 us against floors of 40.0 / 44.2, so neither row is near its floor. WEAKEST LINK: the full decode_1 estimate (-8..-12 us -> 123-126) double-counts. s2's 'custom Q+O 18.6 vs master sans FA3 27.3 us' included dl_o_kernel's prologue 1 absorbing the unpad copies and o_norm_gate (FusedRMSNormGate). The parent's sk two-level kernel already removes FusedRMSNormGate (norm-gate epilogue), so in s3 dl_o runs with prologue 0 and that part of s2's 8.7 us saving is already in the parent's ~134. A realistic A saving vs the parent is ~4-6 us, plus R ~1.2 and unpool ~2.7, so expect ~126-128, not 123-126. The 'not 4 us below parent' kill line is still reachable. Second weak point: the sliding decode_1 row is the only clean B+C attribution, and its kill line (below 122.5, i.e. -1.1% vs 123.9) is inside the 1.5% noise band. Same-code rows drift by 2-4 us between runs (boundaries-unpooler-pdl-small-t, flat, read 123.87 on a 127.48 base; current master reads 123.9). The 87211e13 gain was measured against a 127.48 base, and some of that has since been absorbed by master (w2 atomic-add at T=1 also shortens the decode_1 rows). B+C may come in at ~2-3 us, below the significance threshold. The expected rows for decode_16/32 and verify (flat) match the tokens==1 gating: verify_1 is T=8 and correctly excluded. The headline effect is small (~(16*7 + 46*3)/17775 ≈ 1.4%), but as a rewrite this stage is judged on the replaced kernels' own time. Profile top_kernels at both decode_1 rows (dl_qkv, sk2, dl_o, R, unpool vs nvjet/qk_norm/store_cache/R/nvjet+pad) plus the selector CUDA-event lines make the milestones readable.
confounders: full-decode-sk-ticket-restack-b1-b64 (parent, not yet run): A's saving is measured against whatever the parent's B=1 path ends up being. If the parent's B=1 selector keeps FA3 (sk slower or self-check miss), A must fall back to s2's FA3 + dl_o prologue-1 path, a different composition from the one specified. A full decode_1 gain would then mix 'sk2 absent' with 'Q/O present'. The q layout and gate source also change: dl_qkv writes a contiguous bf16 gate [T,1024], while the parent's norm-gate epilogue reads the gate out of qkv at qkv.stride(0). The sk kernel must be given gate_stride=1024, or a silent wrong-gate read results.

w2-marlin-atomic-add-t1-port: its use_atomic_add path is gated on 'align is not None and dispatch is None' at num_tokens==1, and state['w2_mode'] is chosen by a prepare self-check that runs through kernel R's align. Piece B replaces R. If _w2_atomic_self_check still exercises the old R, or the new R's sorted_ids/n_padded padding differs (e.g. sentinel values for remote -1 slots), w2 can silently switch mode or mis-zero C. Any decode_1 move could then come from the w2 mode flipping rather than from R. Re-run the w2 self-check after the new R is installed, and print w2_mode in the PATH CHOSEN line.

small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl: B adds PDL after P in the P->R chain, and A adds PDL edges qkv->sk2->dl_o into SGLang's non-PDL FusedPostNormResidualPreNorm. PDL overlap savings depend on the neighbouring kernels' prologues, so R's -1.2 us measured on a base without the sk kernel need not transfer. This affects magnitude only, not the sign.
post-expert-norm-triton-small-t: the unpool kernel (C) reads _post_norm_combine_kernel's bf16 output. The layout is unchanged, so this is not a real confounder beyond the unpool's own rel-L2 check.

dense-chain-stage2-attn-side-pdl-t1-gate / stack-route-topk-pdl-unpool-nf1 (sources, not landed): their measured gains were on bases without split-KV and without w2 atomic-add (base 127.48/142.93 vs master 123.9/139.2). Part of their reported delta is therefore base-dependent and already absorbed.
interference: No companion runs are warranted. This is a rewrite stage with three pieces behind separate state flags, and each piece prints a prepare-time CUDA-event selector line (new vs incumbent) plus a PATH CHOSEN line. That gives per-piece attribution inside the single run. The row structure also separates them: sliding decode_1 = B+C, full decode_1 = A+B+C. The one real ambiguity is that the sliding row's B+C effect (~2-4 us) sits at the noise floor. A control for it would be a plain repeat of the already-run 87211e13 code on master, and identical code is never re-run. An ab-revert of w2-marlin-atomic-add-t1-port or of the parent would spend one of the 3 remaining decode checks on a question the selector logs and the self-check already answer. The next stage is the better place to isolate any piece that turns out ambiguous.
rules_flags: The KV store moves into dl_qkv_kernel. It must reproduce store_cache exactly: divide by k_scale/v_scale when kv_scale != 1 (read from the device tensors, not from host values), write slot 0 as a live row (reserved_skip_index=-1), and use the same bf16 rounding before the E4M3 encode. The self-check's 'within one FP8 code' must cover kv_scale 0.25 as well as 1.

Ticket counters and split-K workspaces for dl_qkv, dl_o, sk2 (both levels), R and unpool must all live in the per-state dict and self-reset. The sources kept some of them as module-level buffers (the parent hypothesis itself calls this out), and two states rotate.

The selectors pick a path by timing at prepare on synthetic data. That is allowed (config-gated, decided before kernel_fn), but the gate inside kernel_fn must read only the stored per-state flag and config (tokens==1, window, batch, q_len, page), never a value derived from inputs.

Near-tie top-k in the new R must match SGLang's tie order or stay within the routing tolerance in TASK.md. The self-check covers near-tie cases; make sure that check is on real-weight logits magnitudes, not only synthetic ones.
open_questions: If the parent's B=1 sk selector keeps FA3 (or the parent fails), does piece A fall back to s2's FA3 + dl_o prologue-1 composition, or turn off entirely? The change text specifies only the sk2 composition.

Does the sk two-level kernel accept a separate contiguous gate tensor (stride 1024), or does it hard-code reading the gate from qkv at qkv.stride(0)? dl_qkv writes no bf16 qkv at NF=1 except in 'raw' mode.
The dl_o 6.5 us figure: was it measured with prologue 1 (s2) or prologue 0? At prologue 0, after sk2, the expected saving vs the parent's nvjet o GEMM is the right comparison, not the s2 figure.
Does _w2_atomic_self_check run after the new R is installed, and does the new R emit the same sorted_ids sentinel/padding that Marlin's atomic-add w2 assumes?

Is the sliding decode_1 kill line (122.5) achievable given that 87211e13's -5 us was against a 127.48 base and current master already reads 123.9? Consider judging B+C on their profile kernel times (R 7.0 -> 5.8, unpool+pad 9.2 -> 6.5) rather than the row median.
